verdict:
evidence_table frames as at HEAD 09c4af8. purses is from 8d47b04 and seam from 03dcdd7, both 2560x1440 and unchanged since. The other eleven frames date from 3e022af to efcef77 (motifs). Mean 5.5, lowest 4.5 (materials). Not pro level. Scores unchanged.

The stitch work has moved forward:
- The baked beaded row is gone, and both plates now show one physical row.
- The macro's "7" kink is gone.
- The tracks sit on the thread (median offset about 1 px).
- The clasp is no longer a beacon, though it still holds the frame's single brightest pixel.

Three things keep the chapter-4 pair below a fern film:
1. The tote is still mustard.
   - Purses graded front panel (x1850-2150, y650-850), median of per-pixel Lab: (18.6, 3.5, 13.1), a/b hue 75.2 deg, chroma 13.6.
   - Target is 60-65 deg and 13-14 chroma, so the hue is 10-15 deg too yellow.
   - Raw panel median is RGB (93, 50, 0): BAG_GRADE's sat=1.7 drives blue to 0 on 92% of the panel's pixels.
   - The seam macro reads Lab (14.0, 3.7, 8.6), 66.9 deg, chroma 9.3. That is dull khaki-brown, about dE 6.4 from the purses panel, so the bag changes across the cut.
2. On the macro, the red trace runs over bare leather next to each strap. The track marks these spans visible, but they have no thread:
   - left strap: x 670-725, peak 64 against 62 leather;
   - right strap: x 2030-2103, peak 41 against 36.
   Elsewhere on the macro the thread peaks at about 65-145, at least 30 above the leather.
3. The materials do not hold up at 2560:
   - The tote panel is a textureless flat sheet.
   - The shoulder bag has a wet-vinyl sheen. Its lit flank turns pink-mauve (hue about -4 deg, chroma up to about 11.5, x 545-824, y 566-887) and holds most of the frame's pixels at 90 or above.
   - The satchel body is a black hole (p50 13). Its clasp is flat grey putty, where the prop (TRIPO_PACKAGE: gold clasp and rings) and the lead's gift ruling call for gold.
   - The tote's brass rings and feet grade yellow-green to lime (hue about 76-91 deg). On the macro the rings are the most saturated pixels (chroma up to about 28), with the lit strap faces close behind at about 25. At b5233b2 the same hardware graded about 58-63 deg, so the tote's hue/sat change caused most of this.
   - An olive out-of-focus blob behind the lip at about (1340, 590) on the macro (hue about 105 deg) sits right above the trace's centre. On purses the same spot is a dark knob at about (1980, 500).

Red/maroon check:
- Only the shoulder bag's lit flank on purses carries red-ish colour: 0.4% of the frame, burgundy washed to pink-mauve.
- Seam has about 70-77 stray pixels: nothing.
- The other eleven frames have none. That includes motifs, whose dusty-rose card measures hue about 34 deg at chroma about 7: pastel, not red.

Rest of the stage, scored but not re-judged in detail:
- push, passport and laptop/laptop_before are the strongest.
- overhead's prints and pair/page/screen are deliberately blank graphics plates.
- entries has ruled lines and checkboxes on the forms: form-like but not letter-like, acceptable.
- entries, page, tickets and motifs show bright white scratch streaks on the wood that read as noise.
- motifs (1280x720, published after the last critique) is a clean, unlettered insert.

Note on fixes 2, 3 and 8: tote_topstitch, its thread material and _paint_over_tote_lip live in noir-kit/props.py. scenes/AGENT_BRIEF.md says a stage may not edit noir-kit, so these changes go in a copy inside the stage's own files.

Note on the meshes: each handbag GLB is a single mesh with a single material and texture. No strap, tab, clasp or ring can be hidden or given its own material. Hardware has to be isolated with the GLB's metallic map or with a UV-region retouch.
answers:
1. Does one real stitch line now read across the tabs?
Mostly. Both plates have a single physical row, and the macro's "7" kink is gone.
- Seam: three visible runs (x 0-469, about 725-2030, about 2315-2560) follow one smooth curve through both straps. It runs from y 678 at the left edge to about 721 at the centre and back to 676 at the right edge, and reads as one seam across each strap.
- But the thread stops short of each strap on its inner side: x 670-725 beside the left strap and x 2030-2103 beside the right one. The leather there is lit, and seam.seam.json marks those spans visible (its occluded intervals are 469-670 and 2103-2298), so the red trace will run 55-73 px over bare leather.
- Cause: tote_topstitch drops every stitch whose ray along -front first hits something more than 0.054 m proud of the base, which here is the strap. That is the strap's footprint seen head-on. The seam camera looks at the tote from the left, so the strap actually covers a different span of the hem.
- Purses: continuous at plate scale. Outside the tab intervals (1835-1871, 2111-2147) there are two breaks, both in the straps' black shadow, where neither thread nor leather shows (Y about 6-8):
  - about 20 px at x 1871-1890;
  - about 10 px at x 2148-2157.
  On the right end of the row (x 2160-2310, in the lamp's falloff) the thread is only about 7-9 above the leather.
- The stitches read as uniform near-neutral off-white lozenges, not tobacco waxed thread. Graded chroma is about 4; raw they are warm beige (about 144/120/94, chroma 19), and the film grade washes them out. There are no needle holes and no slant, so at 2560 they look like a dotted CG line rather than saddle stitching.

2. Do any remaining leather creases compete with the stitch line?
Mildly. The creases are not the main problem.
- A soft diagonal fold starts on the stitch line just right of the left strap, about (860, 720) to (820, 850). It is low contrast but begins exactly where the thread starts.
- A band of lumpy dimples sits between the row and the lip edge, at about x 1150-1250 and 1650-2000, y 655-690. It is faint at normal view and plain once boosted. It reads as mesh noise rather than leather. It stays above the line and does not cross it.
- The real competitors are:
  - the olive blob behind the lip at about (1340, 590), directly above the trace's centre;
  - the yellow-green brass rings at the tab tops (hue about 80 deg, chroma up to about 28, the most saturated pixels on the macro);
  - the washed pale-beige lit faces of the straps (p95 about 136/117/102, chroma up to about 25).

3. Do the three bag materials lead the receipt and satchel clasp in the lineup?
Not convincingly.
- Clasp: much quieter (graded p95 about 48-51, only about 130-200 px at or above 60), but it still holds the frame's brightest pixel (110 at 1259, 843).
- Receipt: still matches the tote at the top end. Its p95 is about 74-76 against the tote's 69-71, and its peak 84. It has 3,332 px at or above 75 against the tote's 4,297 from a far larger area. Its white curl on dark wood is the strongest contrast in the right half.
- Shoulder bag: its glossy sheen (max 97) holds most of the frame's pixels at 90 or above. It reads as wet vinyl, and its lit flank goes pink-mauve rather than burgundy.
- Satchel: the body sits at p50 13 and p95 20, so its grain and leather are illegible; it reads only through its grey hardware.
- The tote wins on area, but as a flat mustard sheet.

Tote colour, as the lead asked (coordination/lead.md, 2026-11-28 00:40). Figures are the median of per-pixel Lab:
- Purses: graded hue 75.2 deg against the 60-65 target (fail); chroma 13.6 against 13-14 (pass). Raw panel median (93, 50, 0): blue clipped by sat=1.7.
- Seam: graded hue 66.9 deg, chroma 9.3 (too weak), L 14.0 against 18.6 on purses. The macro does not match its master.
- b5233b2's purses panel (hue 0.50, sat 1.0, val 0.84) measures about 57-60 deg here: 56.4 as median of per-pixel Lab, 57.0 as Lab of the mean RGB, 60.3 as Lab of the median RGB. Chroma is about 13.6, L 20.3. The lead's rounded figures give 63 deg. So that grade sat at or just below the 60 deg floor, not squarely on target. The lighting and the tote's spec and roughness have also changed since.

fixes.problem: The tote is mustard. Purses graded front-panel hue is 75.2 deg (target 60-65), and sat 1.7 clips the raw blue channel to 0 on 92% of the panel. The seam macro panel is 66.9 deg at chroma 9.3 and L 14, about dE 6.4 from the purses master. The same hue/sat push turns the tote's brass hardware yellow-green: about 76-91 deg now against about 58-63 at b5233b2.
fixes.fix:
1. In evidence_table.py, set BAG_GRADE['handbag-tote'] hue/sat/val back to b5233b2's: dict(sat=1.0, val=0.84, hue=0.50, rough_add=0.32). Keep the current rough_add 0.32 and spec 0.08.
2. Expect about 57-60 deg by the median-Lab method above. The lead's rounded figures gave 63 deg for b5233b2, and the lighting has changed since. Report the result, and say which method you used.
3. Re-render both cameras.
4. For seam, raise CAMERAS['seam'] exposure from -1.4 (about -1.0 to -0.8) until the seam panel matches the purses panel: L within about 1, dE under about 3. At b5233b2's grade the seam panel was only L 14.5, so the grade change alone will not close the gap.
5. Check that the raw panel's blue channel stays above about 8.
6. Report graded panel medians for both plates: purses at x1850-2150, y650-850; seam at x900-1800, y800-1200.

fixes.problem: There is no thread beside the inner edge of each strap (x 670-725 and 2030-2103), but the track marks those spans visible, so the red trace will run over bare leather. tote_topstitch drops every stitch whose -front ray first hits something more than 0.054 m proud of the base (here the strap). From this camera angle the strap covers a different span of the hem.
fixes.fix:
1. Copy tote_topstitch into evidence_table_mats.py (for example tote_topstitch_cam); noir-kit is off limits to the stage. The tote is one mesh with one material, so there is no separate strap or tab object to test against.
2. When the first -front hit is more than 0.054 m proud, cast again from just past that hit to reach the panel surface behind the strap, and place the stitch there. Drop it only where that second hit is still proud, which is the tab itself.
3. project_tote_seam already flags whatever the strap hides from each camera as occluded.
4. Call the copy instead of props.tote_topstitch in bags().
5. Re-export seam.seam.json and purses.seam.json. On seam, confirm the thread peaks at least 25 above the leather at every point the track marks visible. On purses, confirm that no visible span outside the straps' black shadow is longer than about 10 px without thread.

fixes.problem: The stitches read as uniform near-neutral lozenges (graded chroma about 4; raw they are warm beige, about 144/120/94, and the film grade washes them out). They are not tobacco saddle thread: no holes and no slant, so at 2560 they look like a dotted CG line.
fixes.fix:
1. In the stage-side copy from fix 2, change the 'waxed linen saddle thread' colour from (0.42,0.33,0.22) to a more saturated tobacco, about (0.30,0.20,0.11).
2. Keep the thread in the 'tote lip graze' receivers. The graze is what makes the row read, and fix 2 needs it at least 25 above the leather. Check that the graded thread keeps chroma of about 8 or more at a warm hue.
3. Slant each stitch: offset the two end points of each 3-point spline by about +/-0.0005 m along the hem's vertical (about 18 deg).
4. Keep the exported track smooth. Build it from the stitch centres, or smooth it, so the red line does not zigzag about 4 px with the slant.
5. Add a needle hole at every stitch end: a dark 0.25 mm dimple about 0.0002 m into the leather.

fixes.problem: An olive out-of-focus blob sits behind the lip at about (1340,590) on seam (hue about 105 deg); on purses it is a dark knob at about (1980,500). The tab rings and the tote's feet grade yellow-green to lime (hue about 76-91 deg). On the macro the rings are the most saturated pixels, at chroma up to about 28.
fixes.fix:
1. Re-measure after fix 1. At b5233b2's grade the same hardware graded about 58-63 deg, so the revert should remove most of the green.
2. If the rings, feet or blob still grade above about 70 deg or above chroma 15, recolour them through the tote's single material. The GLB has no separate parts to hide or re-material. Use the metallic map as a mask, or a UV-region retouch like the lip retouch, as a stage-side copy. Mix the hardware's base colour toward aged brass (about 0.36,0.22,0.09) at roughness about 0.45.
3. Target: graded hue 60-70 deg, chroma 12 or less.
4. Darken the blob's texel region toward the lining or leather so nothing bright sits above the trace's centre.

fixes.problem: The receipt matches the tote's highlights (p95 about 74-76 against 69-71, peak 84), and its white curl is the strongest contrast in the right half.
fixes.fix:
1. Darken the receipt_c4 thermal material from (0.16,0.165,0.17) to about (0.10,0.10,0.105), and/or move receipt_c4 about 4-5 cm further toward +x and -y, into the front cutter's falloff. Keep the whole curl in frame.
2. Target: graded receipt p95 of 55 or less, at least 15 below the tote panel's p95.

fixes.problem: The shoulder bag reads as wet vinyl. Its lit flank washes to pink-mauve (graded hue about -4 deg, chroma up to about 11.5, x545-824, y566-887) and holds most of the frame's pixels at 90 or above. The lead's gift ruling keeps it burgundy, and red as a mark belongs only to the trace.
fixes.fix:
1. In BAG_GRADE['handbag-shoulder'], lower the finish spec from 0.35 to about 0.12 and raise rough_add from 0.25 to about 0.42.
2. Do not shift its hue toward violet or plum: it must stay the burgundy gift.
3. If the flank still reads pink rather than dark burgundy, lower val (0.55 to about 0.45) instead. Target: graded chroma 8 or less and max below the tote's.

fixes.problem: The satchel body is a black void (p50 13, p95 20), and its pebble grain cannot be seen. Its clasp is flat grey putty rather than the prop's gold, yet it still holds the frame max (110 at 1259,843). The cause is that the satchel is one mesh with one material, so BAG_GRADE's ceiling (0.038,0.033,0.024) and metal_limit 0.10 flatten the clasp along with the leather.
fixes.fix:
1. The ceiling caps the base colour, so raising val from 0.25 to 0.33 alone will barely lift the body. Raise the ceiling as well (to about 0.05).
2. Get some light onto the satchel's flap edge so the body's p50 reaches 18-22 and the grain shows in the rim. Either restrict 'bag edge return' to the satchel and raise it from 2.2 to about 3.5, or use a separate small light. It currently also lights the shoulder bag, which fix 6 is calming.
3. For a gold clasp, use the GLB's metallic map as a mask in a stage-side tune_prop variant:
   - exempt those texels from the ceiling;
   - give them aged brass (about 0.30,0.20,0.09) at roughness 0.4-0.5;
   - cap metallic at about 0.5 (not the 0.10 that also greys the clasp).
   Earlier passes found the shinier clasp read as crumpled foil. Keep its graded p95 at 55 or less and its peak below the tote's.
4. Tell the lead if the clasp goes gold. hongkong_street C34 (lead.md, 03:40) currently relies on this satchel's grey fittings to tell it from the shop satchel's gold, and inspection_room's satchel must match.

fixes.problem: A soft diagonal fold starts on the stitch row at about (860,720)-(820,850), and lumpy dimples sit between the row and the lip edge (x 1150-1250 and 1650-2000, y 655-690): mesh noise, not leather. The panel is also a flat, textureless sheet on both plates.
fixes.fix:
1. Widen the lip retouch locally with a stage-side copy of _paint_over_tote_lip in evidence_table_mats.py. Flatten the tote normal map to (0.5,0.5,1.0) from the lip edge down to about 12 mm below the stitch row, which covers the fold's lower end.
2. Add leather texture to the whole panel at two scales:
   - a fine grain bump (noise or Voronoi at about 0.4 mm, strength about 0.05) for the macro;
   - a very soft low-frequency value and roughness variation (about 1-3 cm) so the panel stops reading as a flat sheet at purses scale.
3. Keep the variation broad and blotch-free, so nothing reads as a stamp or a mark.
